requirements.title: One managed harness channel, with proved turn boundaries
requirements.spec: Behavioural. WHEN Lys starts a session requiring context actions or goal delivery, THE SYSTEM SHALL select a versioned managed-control adapter and bind it to the runner session, proved process start identity and actual harness conversation identity before accepting control operations. Extend DIRECTORY-050's Launch/session transport with a managed-pipe mode; its existing PTY mode remains available for manual sessions, but a profile requiring these controls refuses control_transport_unsupported on PTY-only sessions. Never silently restart or migrate a running terminal session. The managed process runs under the same isolated home, environment, credentials, process ownership and policy as the normal runner launch. Keep 051's hooks, usage collector, cursor accounting, budget/goal stores and operations log; do not create a second usage or reminder system. All session inputs, including the person's messages and automation, pass through one dispatcher so a turn cannot start between a boundary check and control dispatch. Map started/completed/compaction events to a typed event projection with source identity, session generation, conversation and turn identifiers. Subscribe other consumers (including 065) through this one reader, with durable cursors and a named gap when transient evidence was not retained. Hook callbacks enqueue and return; they never wait for the turn that invoked them to end. Events from another generation cannot open a boundary. A reconnect starts in unknown boundary state until authoritative harness state is reconciled. A transport loss is visible; silence is never an idle signal. Version/executable and capability evidence are recorded from the actual launched binary, not inferred from a source checkout.

requirements.title: Use Claude and Codex control protocols, never terminal typing
requirements.spec: Behavioural. WHEN the dispatcher delivers an act, THE SYSTEM SHALL use a machine protocol over runner-owned pipes, with no PTY write, terminal key, shell command construction or external terminal-control application. Claude's adapter launches the selected binary with --print --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --replay-user-messages, an explicit bound session and the existing isolated settings. Send one SDK user envelope with a stable uuid, session_id, parent_tool_use_id null, and message role user/content. A normal result closes a submitted turn; partial assistant text does not. A compaction request is the exact /compact command in this protocol, never terminal text. Discover compact capability from system/init slash_commands. Confirm actual compaction only on that session's system/compact_boundary, not a result success: the documented no-history case succeeds without compacting. User-envelope replay with matching uuid confirms message admission only; it does not prove completion, obedience or goal satisfaction. Validate these wire fixtures against the actual installed Claude version before enabling the adapter; absent required envelope correlation refuses the capability. Codex's adapter owns one app-server stdio child and JSON-RPC initialize/initialized handshake, creates or resumes the explicit bound thread, sends thread/compact/start with threadId and delivers a reminder through turn/start with threadId, clientUserMessageId and input text. The compact response is acceptance only; require the corresponding completed ContextCompaction item and terminal turn observation before declaring compaction complete. A turn/start reply identifies the admitted turn, not a finished goal. Only dispatch while the owned thread is idle; never use turn/steer to inject mid-turn. Resolve server approval requests through the existing policy authority; never automatically approve one to keep the transport moving. Unknown protocol variants or missing proof yield a named unsupported/uncertain state. Preserve existing permissions when starting turns: no sandbox or approval override in a reminder call. The local inspected Codex contract is codex-channels 7cbba483, app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs and v2/{thread,turn,item}.rs and app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs. A checkout is a fixture source, not installed-binary proof. No app-server function is attributed to legacy notify; notify remains after-turn only.

requirements.title: Enforce context thresholds at the owned boundary
requirements.spec: Behavioural. WHEN 051's authoritative context measurement crosses its held threshold, THE SYSTEM SHALL reuse its stable crossing/operation identity and block release of the next normal input before running the configured compact or stop act. Use 051's measurement validity and budget precedence; repeated snapshots are not new crossings. A compact command waits for the active turn to finish, then runs before queued normal input. The context watch must not recursively react to its own compaction events. After actual compaction, require a fresh measurement below the threshold before releasing held input. When compaction fails, is unsupported, finishes above threshold or yields no valid post-measurement, keep the next turn held and show the named reason, without automatic repeated compaction. The responsible person can choose the existing stop act or an authorised policy change; the agent cannot lift its own hold. A configured stop uses the existing proved process/session owner and exit receipt, never a typed stop command; stop confirmation requires actual process exit. Explicit stop takes priority over queued compaction/reminders. Tracking loss under a required context policy holds the next turn instead of assuming the limit was respected. Setting a threshold is an authorised product policy, not a request timeout or watchdog.

requirements.title: Deliver current goal and reminder words at turn boundaries
requirements.spec: Behavioural. WHEN a 051 reminder occurrence is due for an authorised live session, THE SYSTEM SHALL enqueue its existing stable occurrence and goal version for the same dispatcher. On the first permitted boundary, re-read the current goal state/version and visibility before dispatch. Marked-met, dropped, cancelled or revoked items do not send stale queued words. Updated words replace an unsent occurrence's payload under a recorded revision without inventing a new due occurrence. Delivered content contains the named goal/expectation/deliverable, exact saved words, due instant and time left or lateness; preserve text as data with proper JSON encoding. Team delivery names each intended session and tracks its receipt separately so one unavailable member does not block the others. Idle means no active harness turn; a goal reminder may start the next controlled turn then. An active tool call is not a boundary. A compaction-triggered reminder waits for completion of compaction and release of the context hold; it does not enter the summary operation. A reminder reaching a stopped session is visibly undeliverable and does not secretly relaunch an agent. Reuse 051 timers, late occurrence handling and authority, without a second scheduler, polling or external message app. Text is delivered as a Lys reminder with recorded provenance; it cannot become an arbitrary slash command. In Claude, prefix an ordinary reminder envelope with the fixed plain-text label Lys reminder before the saved text, so a saved /compact line is data, not a command. Codex uses typed text input. Receipt means harness admission, never proof that the agent did the requested work.

requirements.title: Reconcile uncertain delivery with existing operation receipts
requirements.spec: Behavioural. WHEN delivery starts, THE SYSTEM SHALL persist the existing 051 operation identity and a prepared request before a pipe write, then record accepted, confirmed, refused or uncertain as evidence arrives. Persist the distinction between safely unsent and possibly sent; after a crash in the write/receipt gap, do not replay or mint a replacement merely because no answer is stored. A matching durable harness observation may reconcile the original operation; a request UUID is correlation, not an unsupported exactly-once claim. For Codex, use available typed thread/item history or persisted observed events; a transient event gap stays uncertain. For Claude, reconcile matching saved admission/completion evidence for the explicit session; never read arbitrary other transcript files. If no authoritative readback exists, leave uncertain and expose an explicit responsible-person reconciliation action on that operation, which records the person's decision and never silently resends. A decision to send again creates a distinct authorised occurrence labelled possible prior delivery; it must pass the same boundary and authority checks. A restarted runner does not claim a dead pipe restored: use 050's actual lifecycle state and only resume a conversation through a separately authorised session start. Snapshot-backed folds and cursor reads preserve the repository's bounded-restart invariant. Goal text stays under holder visibility; exported operational telemetry contains identifiers/states only, never the text or credentials.

requirements.title: Plain controls and a real managed-session proof
requirements.spec: Behavioural. WHEN the responsible person opens 051's Usage page, THE SYSTEM SHALL extend that page in place with current context limit/action, observed value and coverage, held/active context state, pending/accepted/uncertain control operations, saved goals/reminders and their due/delivery state. Reuse its forms, routes, authorisation and stores; do not create a second dashboard. Show managed-control capability on the agent/session page before launch and explain unsupported sessions in plain words. Saved settings persist after reload. Exercise both actual launched harnesses on Dean in scratch homes: enter a goal and reminder in the browser, cause a turn-boundary delivery, and separately cause a valid context crossing, actual compaction and stop. Keep a pipe trace stripped of saved text/credentials, terminal-writer count, source event identifiers, before/after context evidence, operation receipts and process-exit evidence. Mock fixtures cover faults but cannot substitute for the live two-harness proof. If an installed harness cannot supply the required protocol, return a named blocker and keep that acceptance incomplete rather than claiming a fixture as live evidence. Browser proof is a controlled scratch install, not a production install. Argus may be absent for every proof.

boundaries: SHALL NOT send compaction, context notices, goals or reminders through a PTY, terminal keyboard API, pasted command or shell expansion.
SHALL NOT duplicate 051 usage accounting, budget/goal stores, scheduler or Usage screen.

amendments.subject: R1: the managed child is made a session leader by a lys runner child-entry subcommand
amendments.ruling: A PTY child is a session leader through portable-pty; a pipe child of std::process::Command is not, and pty.rs end_member and the stop cleanup prove the leader by getsid and getpgid. The runner's containment entry binary is used by tests only and nothing installs it, so a new binary would be install work. amendments.ruling: Archie's read of BOX 18 (17:44) found that selecting the managed transport from an agent's limits or reminders, with no adapter yet qualified, would stop every such agent starting after the install. amendments.subject: R5's explicit resend is a Line::Resent folded by the goals owner, and the goals snapshot kind moves to lys-goals-state/v2
amendments.ruling: goals_state.rs fire() advances the reminder's timer for every Fired (lines 550 to 570), so a resend cannot be a Fired. A responsible person's decision to send again appends a new Line::Resent carrying the new Fired and the prior operation id. The existing goals owner folds it: the new occurrence is distinct, under its own operation id, keeps the prior identity so the possible-prior-delivery label survives a snapshot recovery, leaves that timer's next_due unchanged, and records no compaction event. A resend passes the same boundary and authority checks as any send, and one refused at the boundary records nothing. Narrowing resend to existing operation identities is refused: R5 requires a distinct authorised occurrence. An old install's goals log holds no Resent line, so its leaves read unchanged and need no forward migration. The folded snapshot's shape changes, so FORMAT in goals_state.rs moves from lys-goals-state/v1 to lys-goals-state/v2, and the existing refusal of another kind rebuilds the fold from the leaves, as the budgets log did in tonight's proof. Rollback is DIRECTORY-082's: the put-back restores data.previous, so an old build never reads a Resent line. Tests: an old-kind goals snapshot is refused by kind and rebuilt with every goal and timer kept; a Resent survives a reopen with its label; next_due is unchanged by a Resent; a Resent refused at the boundary records nothing. The upgrade proof writes one Resent in the window. The Operations owner's permanent used-id guard stays whole; its checkpoint cost is measured and posted with the implementation chosen (Brisket e85b2b03; Waffles 6ca66f07).

amendments.subject: R5's operations checkpoint is triggered in proportion to its own size, never by a fixed count
amendments.ruling: The operations owner checkpoints by borrowing its folded projection, with no whole-state clone. It syncs the journal before it replaces the checkpoint outside the table lock, and at start it reads one checkpoint and folds only the tail after it (Brisket 1baebfad). The permanent used-id guard stays whole. The checkpoint is taken when the journal tail since the last checkpoint holds at least as many bytes as that checkpoint. A fixed count of transitions is refused: Brisket's figures show a checkpoint of 45 MB at 1 million used ids, so a fixed trigger costs 45 MB / N per operation, growing with the guard for good, the write amplification Tom asked about at 19:04. A proportional trigger keeps total bytes written within about twice the bytes kept, and a start replays at most one checkpoint's worth of tail, never all history. It is the size of the thing kept, not a timer or a constant, as ADR-001 allows. Tests: after K operations, journal plus checkpoint bytes written are at most twice the bytes kept plus one checkpoint; a reopen replays no more tail than the last checkpoint's size; the used-id guard is whole after a reopen at every boundary; a crash between the journal sync and the checkpoint replace reopens on the old checkpoint and its full tail. The handback names the proportional rule and shows the written-bytes bound, posts the final typed projection's encode, replace and decode cost at 1 thousand, 10 thousand, 100 thousand and 1 million used ids, and gives the table-lock hold at a checkpoint and the start read on the final shape at 100 thousand and 1 million. The rule bounds what is written, not what is kept: the used-id guard still grows by one id per operation for good, and that is a later storage box, not this one (Archie 0f0c729d; Waffles b56bb01f, 265ebe9d).

amendments.subject: R5 names operations/store.rs and operations/control.rs, the two operations test paths, and the v1 migration fixture they keep
amendments.ruling: The operations owner splits whole items into operations/store.rs (the journal, the proportional checkpoint of amendment 17, the used-id guard and the v1 forward migration) and operations/control.rs (prepared requests, certainty and the identifier-only control receipt), declared from operations.rs. tests/operations.rs (line 238) and tests/operations_index/cases.rs (lines 44 to 88) are tied to the v1 operations.jsonl name and raw outcome lines; they move to the new journal and checkpoint, and their deduplication, torn-tail, append-only and interrupted-operation assertions stay as strong as they are. No assertion is weakened, no test is ignored and no v1 writer is kept. One v1 fixture stays, written as the old build wrote operations.jsonl, with a torn tail and an interrupted operation: it is the forward migration's input. The tests prove that the migration at open carries every outcome over, keeps the interrupted operation uncertain, writes nothing back in v1 form, and does not migrate again on a second open (Brisket 3d6ae80c; Waffles 864316c5).

amendments.subject: R4 and R5 name the control children of goals_state, goals_store, goals_api and receipts_api, and R5 names runner_sessions.rs for the control receipt's kind
amendments.ruling: So that no file passes the 500-line limit, the control work moves into whole-item children of its existing owners, each declared from its parent, with no second store, loop or owner. goals_state/control.rs holds the current-control and index reads and the Resent validation, goals_store/control.rs holds the resend append and its rendering, and goals_api/control.rs holds the boundary reminder judgement and the explicit reconciliation and resend route, and receipts_api/control.rs holds the current-controls readback and the reconciliation endpoints. runner_sessions.rs kind() (line 275) gains one arm for the ControlReceipt answer, and one for a ControlReceipts page if one is added; driven() stays untouched as ruled (Brisket 65bd921a; Waffles 2bb8cb97).

amendments.subject: R5's migration carries every interrupted v1 Accepted or Delivering operation over as Uncertain, and the restart assertion at tests/operations.rs line 259 reads Uncertain instead of Refused
amendments.ruling: harness_control/events.rs managed_written (lines 343 to 371) sets a Delivering operation to Accepted only after its pipe write succeeded, so an installed v1 Accepted may already have been sent. Reading it as Refused tells the person it never happened, and that invites a second delivery. So the migration carries every interrupted v1 Accepted or Delivering operation over as Uncertain, with a private control record whose preparation is named absent and whose certainty is possibly_sent. No request id, frame or admission is invented, and nothing is replayed. The assertion at tests/operations.rs line 259 that expected the v1 Accepted operation Refused now expects it Uncertain, with that named lack-of-preparation evidence. This is a stronger check, not a narrowed one. Three cases are added beside it: a migrated legacy Uncertain is never resent on its own and offers the responsible person's decision; that decision passes the same boundary and authority checks as any resend; a newly prepared SafelyUnsent operation still reads Refused and is kept (Brisket d81030d7; Waffles bfb64be0).

amendments.subject: budgets_state/control.rs and protocol/acts.rs are whole-item children for the length limit, and the other moved methods go into files R3 to R5 already name
amendments.ruling: By the repository's count_rust scanner, before fmt, budgets_state.rs reaches 590 code lines with the current control_context method, protocol.rs 502, harness_control/events.rs 557, harness_control.rs 518 and goals_api.rs 524. Each is brought under the limit by moving whole items to a child of the same owner, never by splitting a function, and nothing is reworded on the way. budgets_state/control.rs holds the whole current_control_context method (R3). protocol/acts.rs holds the whole existing Act enum, re-exported from protocol.rs. Moving the enum changes no wire byte: an existing round-trip or golden test of Act's encoding passes unchanged, and if none exists, one is added before the move. Sessions::apply_boundary_reply moves whole into harness_control/context.rs (R3), Pending::new into harness_control/reminders.rs (R4), the goals_state index reads into goals_state/control.rs and the whole Live Deliver implementation into goals_api/control.rs (amendment 19). No owner, scheduler, watcher or history scan is added (Brisket 39a02750; Waffles acb5ea15).

amendments.subject: R5: an Uncertain operation never expires before the responsible person's decision is recorded
amendments.ruling: crates/lys-runner/src/operations.rs keeps a terminal outcome for RETAIN_MS, 24 hours (line 46): fold() puts it into expires at its at plus 24 hours (lines 331 to 332), and prune() (lines 343 to 352) then removes it from held, texts and compacting, while its id stays in seen and is refused operation_repeated as expired (lines 354 to 361). That rule came before BOX 20 (Pikelet 84c5e348, 1 October). terminal() (lines 189 to 195) counts Uncertain as terminal, so an Uncertain operation would leave held after a day, and the responsible-person reconciliation action R5 requires on that operation would be lost. An Uncertain operation therefore never enters expires until the person's decision on it is recorded; once recorded, it follows the same rule as any other terminal outcome. This covers the legacy Uncertain operations migrated under amendment 20. The test: an Uncertain outcome older than 24 hours still offers the decision after a reopen, and its id is not refused as expired. The 24 hour rule for every other outcome is held for Tom, as an age-based removal: unchanged, not extended and not dropped. Taking open_at's supplied instant on restart, instead of the wall clock, is right (Archie 0225afbd; Waffles 640704fd).

amendments.subject: R4 and R5 name operations/delivery.rs: a prepared control's retry is compared against a digest of the original ask
amendments.ruling: operations/delivery.rs accept (lines 42 to 56) compares a retry's text digest with the held outcome's text. Preparation may replace that text with the current boundary words, so an identical retry of the original ask would be refused operation_reused. The private Control record keeps one digest of the original ask, captured before preparation replaces Outcome.text, and accept compares a prepared control's retry against that digest. No words are exported, nothing is replayed and no owner is added. Tests: the identical original ask after current-word preparation reads the original receipt; a changed ask under the same operation id is still refused operation_reused. Waffles asked for this beside amendment 22, which was already pushed, so it stands as its own amendment (Brisket 2d448866; Waffles 4608151d).

amendments.subject: R5 and R6 read the session's control through ControlStatus and a ControlReceipts page, identifiers only
amendments.ruling: R6 shows held and active context state and pending, accepted and uncertain control operations. It reads them through two runner shapes, whose Act and Answer arms live in protocol/acts.rs (amendment 21) and which receipts_api/control.rs serves (amendment 19). ControlStatus gains phase, a closed set (unknown, idle, reserved, active, closed); the active operation id; and the last applied context decision with a named reason code from a closed set. Act::ControlReceipts {session, after} answers Answer::ControlReceipts {page} from Operations.by_session, never a scan of all operations or of history; tracking_store::PAGE_MAX bounds a page, never the total, and every page but the last returns the cursor to resume from. Both answers carry identifiers, states, reason codes and digests only: never a threshold, words or a saved ask. An Uncertain entry is labelled unconfirmed, and a legacy one also preparation absent (amendment 20). Tests: a page holds no more than PAGE_MAX and resumes exactly from after, with no gap and no repeat; a session with more than PAGE_MAX receipts is read whole across pages; a session with no operations answers an empty page by name; an unknown session is refused by name; no field of either answer carries a threshold, words or a saved ask; an unknown phase is reported unknown, never guessed (Brisket e9c621a0; Archie 8012da23; Waffles 4b40e85e, 0a0c4d0d).

amendments.subject: R5's proportional-checkpoint test stays as it is, a migration-seeded test is added beside it, and its 4.445 s is a named slow defect held for Tom
amendments.ruling: proportional_checkpoints_bound_rewrite_bytes_and_keep_every_spent_id in tests/operations_index/cases.rs took 4.445 s on Dean, spending it on about 80 real durability fences plus the checkpoint fences (Brisket 4ec8bc0a). Replacing it with migration-seeded ids, or shrinking its K, would take operations off the normal append path that amendment 17's "after K operations" claim names, and Tom's 23:10 rule says nothing is narrowed overnight. So: (1) the existing test stays exactly as it is, with 1,200 real appends, its fences and all its assertions; (2) a new test is added beside it, with the same 1,200 spent ids seeded by the real migration, then large record updates crossing several proportional boundaries, every guard checked and a final reopen, with the byte and tail invariants; (3) the 4.445 s goes in the handback as a named slow defect, HELD FOR TOM, with its cause and the proposal. A further real-path test with a small starting checkpoint, firing the trigger at least three times, may be added for a faster signal, but it replaces nothing. A fixed count stays refused (Archie 016f02d8; Waffles d98ad5fd withdrawn where it differed, 9d61c090).

amendments.subject: R5: the control readers ask Act::ControlStatus, a direct query that reads no history and keeps Status's reserved control slot
amendments.ruling: The control readers in budgets_act/control.rs, goals_api/control.rs and receipts_api/control.rs asked Act::Status, whose SessionView clones and serializes the session's whole account-move history to answer a question about current control. Act::ControlStatus {session} and Answer::ControlStatus {session, control} are added in protocol/acts.rs; Sessions::control_status in harness_control/context.rs answers them and takes no history and no output lock; socket/acts.rs dispatches the act directly; runner_sessions.rs kind() gains one arm for the answer, and driven() stays untouched. Those three readers switch to it. Act::Status and SessionView stay exactly as they are for every other caller, and nothing is removed from them. Act::Status today takes the reserved control slot, in socket/connection.rs Command::control (line 117) and in dial.rs control_request (line 177), so it is not queued behind ordinary acts. Act::ControlStatus is recognised in both places the same way, so moving a reader off Status does not take that slot from it; R5 therefore modifies socket/connection.rs and dial.rs. Tests: the control answer carries the same control fields SessionView carries for the same session, read side by side; an unknown session is refused by name; reading control_status for a session with a long account-move history does not touch that history, shown with a counter or an allocation bound, never a time; and Act::ControlStatus is classified as a control act in both connection.rs and dial.rs (Brisket ca25e7ba; Waffles 95f19c8b; the slot, Archie).

amendments.subject: R5 pages an agent's control sessions from a derived agent-to-session set in the Runtime index, never from a scan of every session
amendments.ruling: GET /agents/{id}/runtime/sessions filters every held session to find one agent's (runtime_api.rs agent_sessions, lines 386 to 393), so reusing it for the control view would scan every agent's history on each reload. Instead, GET /agents/{id}/control-sessions?after answers at most tracking_store::PAGE_MAX (256) session ids with the cursor to resume from, stopped sessions included so that old uncertainty stays reachable. The endpoint lives in receipts_api/control.rs. It reads an agent-to-ordered-session-position set held in the Runtime Index (runtime_state.rs), through a borrowed selector in the new runtime_state/control.rs: no Tracked or report is cloned, nothing scans all history, and no IO happens under the guard. The set is derived, never stored: it is built in the existing From<Records> pass at open beside positions and live, kept current on the same paths that already change the Index, and adds no stored shape, no format change, no second fold and no extra pass over the log. The route admits exactly as /agents/{id}/runtime/sessions does: a signed caller who sees the agent, refused AgentNotVisible otherwise. Its OpenAPI entry and types go in openapi_table.rs and openapi_runner_types.rs, which every HTTP route amendment 19 gave receipts_api/control.rs also needs (tests/openapi.rs every_declared_route_has_an_entry_and_every_entry_a_route and every_route_names_the_types_it_takes_and_answers); R5 therefore modifies both. Tests: more than 256 sessions are read whole across pages with no gap and no repeat; an unknown cursor and another agent's cursor are refused by name; the number of sessions read is bounded by the page size against a large unrelated history; after a reopen the set equals the one built live, stopped sessions included; a caller who does not see the agent is refused AgentNotVisible; the existing runtime routes answer byte for byte as before, with a check added if none exists. The handback names the set's memory cost: one position per session, and the figure at 10,000 and 100,000 sessions (Brisket 07f12b68; Waffles 7c8ff43b; the admission and OpenAPI files, Archie).

amendments.subject: R5: an uncertain prior is resent at most once, and a failed decision write is finished, never resent
amendments.ruling: The explicit resend route appends the Resent through the goal store, then records the person's decision on the original receipt as a second write. If that write fails, or the service stops between the two, the prior stays Uncertain and unreconciled. A retry under the same operation id re-answers the kept firing, but check_resent refused only a reused occurrence or delivery id, never a prior that already had a Resent, so a resend under a new operation id would deliver the reminder twice (read at Brisket 1f4de95b, goals_state/control.rs lines 10 to 52 and goals_api/control.rs line 356). Amendment 16's Resent is therefore one per uncertain prior. check_resent refuses a prior that already has a Resent, by name, naming the kept occurrence, through a prior-to-occurrence entry in the derived goals index built in the same fold, with no stored shape added. The route, given such a prior, finishes the missing decision for the kept occurrence instead of resending. Tests: after the decision write fails following the append, a resend under a new operation id is refused naming the kept occurrence and exactly one delivery is pending; the same holds after a reopen; a retry under the same operation id still records the decision (Archie e1e45681; Waffles b3decc7e).

amendments.subject: R5: GET /agents/{id}/control-sessions refuses an unknown or foreign cursor with 400, as a server refusal, never through the runner mapping
amendments.ruling: A cursor the caller sends that the service cannot resume from is the caller's error, and every existing cursor refusal in the server answers 400. list_page.rs refuses a cursor that does not decode, or that belongs to another list or filter, as RequestMalformed (lines 95 to 109), which error_status.rs maps to 400 (line 221); and the runner's own cursor_ahead maps to 400 in runner_status (error_status.rs line 281). The control-sessions page is answered by the server from its own Runtime index (amendment 27), not by a runner, so its refusals do not travel as ServerError::Runner, whose unlisted names fall to 409 by design (error_status.rs lines 273 to 285). An unknown cursor and another agent's cursor are each refused as RequestMalformed, with words that name which, at 400, and the route's OpenAPI entry lists RequestMalformed. The cursor test keeps its 400 expectation and its assertions; the route is changed to match the test, never the test to match the route (Brisket 34b9ac77; Waffles d0ccac6f).

amendments.subject: R5's audit sync-count test keeps its 1,024 real appends, a batch-seeded test is added beside it, and its 19.765 s is a named slow defect held for Tom
amendments.ruling: The person-reconciliation handback must name the existing service audit owner's filesystem sync cost. Brisket measured it with lys-log-store's flush-counts feature around ActStore::keep: of 1,024 append calls, 1,023 cost one real sync_all each and the checkpoint call cost three (journal, snapshot file and directory). The test passes and takes 19.765 s on Dean, spent on those real syncs (Brisket f173ae99). As with amendment 25, and under Tom's rule that nothing is narrowed overnight: (1) the 1,024-call test stays exactly as written, with its 1,023-by-one and checkpoint-by-three assertions. It alone shows that no real append before the checkpoint costs more than one sync, which is what would catch a periodic snapshot or a stray directory sync at, say, the 256th or 512th append; the faster fixture proposed in its place proves less and does not replace it. (2) That fixture is added beside it as a second test: one ordinary append asserting exactly one sync; the remaining 1,022 valid audit leaves seeded through the existing FrontierLog::append_batch, asserting the batch costs exactly one durable flush; a reopen from the existing snapshot and tail; then the 1,024th act asserting exactly three syncs, that the checkpoint fired because the tail reached checkpoint size (amendment 17), and that all 1,024 leaves survive the reopen. Seeding and reopening reach the 1,024th by a different tail and snapshot path from the real one, which is why it cannot stand in for test (1). (3) The 19.765 s is a named slow defect, HELD FOR TOM beside amendment 25's 4.445 s, with its cause and the second test as the proposal. The handback names both tests' file paths and both timings; at Brisket's pushed 1f4de95b neither test exists yet. Whether the 1,024-call test leaves the normal checks is Tom's decision, not this box's (Brisket f173ae99; Waffles 18704a94; amendment 25).

amendments.subject: Amendment 30 corrected: the audit store's checkpoint is its existing fixed SNAPSHOT_EVERY count, and the seeded test asserts that rule, not amendment 17's
amendments.ruling: Amendment 30 required the seeded audit test to show the checkpoint fired "because the tail reached checkpoint size (amendment 17)". That is wrong. The audit owner the test measures, ActStore::keep in runner_acts.rs, writes its snapshot when the leaves since the last one reach lys_identity::SNAPSHOT_EVERY, 1,024 (lines 203 to 207); amendment 17's proportional byte rule belongs to the lys-runner operations journal, which has its own tests. BOX 20 changes neither owner's rule. The seeded test therefore asserts: the reopened tail holds 1,023 leaves after the batch; the 1,024th act makes 1,024 since the last snapshot, fires the audit snapshot by that count and costs exactly three syncs; and a reopen holds all 1,024 leaves with an empty tail. Everything else in amendment 30 stands: the 1,024-call test is kept exactly as written, both tests are in crates/lys-identity-server/tests/control_receipts.rs, and the 19.765 s is held for Tom. That the audit store snapshots on a fixed leaf count, the form amendment 17 refused for the operations journal, is recorded as FOUND for a later box and not changed here (Brisket a5b426e8; Archie, from runner_acts.rs on main).

amendments.subject: R5 and R6: GET /goals/{goal}/resends/{prior} names an uncertain prior's kept occurrence, so a reloaded page finishes it and never asks a second delivery
amendments.ruling: After a resend whose decision write failed (amendment 28), a reloaded page has lost the kept occurrence's id. A new id is rightly refused goal_prior_already_resent, but the kept id is only in the refusal's words, and nothing typed lets the page finish it (Brisket b73212d9). GET /goals/{goal}/resends/{prior}, in goals_api/control.rs, answers {goal, prior, occurrence: null | {operation, session}} from the derived prior-to-occurrence index of amendment 28, through one borrowed lookup exposed by goals_store/control.rs: identifiers only, no firing or history scan, no stored shape, no watcher, loop or write. It admits only the active signed-in person who is the goal's current responsible person, judged before anything is read; anyone else is refused by name with nothing about the prior revealed. An unknown goal or a prior that is not an uncertain delivery of that goal is refused by name, never answered null; null means the prior is uncertain and has no kept occurrence. Its OpenAPI entry and types go in openapi_table.rs and openapi_runner_types.rs beside the resend route (amendment 27), and the resend route's existing entry adds goal_prior_already_resent to its listed refusals, which it now answers (409, amendment 28). R6 asks this read when the explicit resend action opens: given an occurrence it offers only to finish that occurrence's decision under its original id and session, and offers a new occurrence only when the read answers null. Tests: another person is refused before any lookup, so a refusal reveals nothing about whether a resend exists; after a failed decision write and a reopen the read names the same kept occurrence; a prior with no resend answers occurrence null, live and after a reopen; an unknown prior is refused by name; and in R6, a reload followed by the resend action retries that same id and never asks a second delivery. The handback states its cost: one index lookup, one borrowed firing, zero syncs. Discovering the occurrence by attempting a write and reading the refusal's words is refused as a design, and so is adding the field to an existing answer, whose wire bytes are already proven (Brisket b73212d9; Waffles dd183d9b).

amendments.subject: R4: a confirmed compaction fires the existing GoalEvent::Compaction once per holder, team holders found by a bounded walk of current compaction holders, and hold() moves whole into goals_state/fold.rs
amendments.ruling: budgets_feed's Body::Operation records budget state and goal delivery answers only, so no compaction reaches an On(Compaction) reminder (Brisket 59c87b10). The existing outcome fold is extracted whole into a tested GoalStore control-answer method in goals_store/control.rs, which R4 now also names. Only a Confirmed Compact or ContextCompact counts; an accepted, uncertain or person-resent operation never does. The feed's session and machine are checked by a point Runtime lookup first. Each eligible holder's reminder keeps one Evented under a stable event id derived from the confirmed operation, so a replayed or repeated feed answer fires nothing new, before or after a reopen. The goals index keeps the current active, open Compaction-reminder holders, maintained by the same fold, with no stored shape added. Agent holders are selected directly. Team holders are found by walking only those current compaction team holders, with one borrowed Team point read each for the agent's current membership; no member list, whole-team clone or fired history is read. Current authority is checked again outside the Goal lock before the append. TeamStore has no reverse membership index and is not widened here: that walk is accepted for BOX 20 because it is bounded by current compaction team holders, never by history, and the handback states the holders visited per compaction at 10 and 1,000 such holders. A reverse membership index is FOUND for a later box. The completion rule stands as R4 wrote it: the reminder waits for compaction to complete and the context hold to release. goals_state.rs is at its 500-line limit, so its whole hold() method moves into the new goals_state/fold.rs, with declarations and re-exports only in the parent, no change in meaning and nothing reworded; the diff shows it as a pure move, and every file stays within 500 lines. Tests: a confirmed compaction fires each eligible agent and team holder's reminder exactly once; the same confirmed operation answered again fires nothing, live and after a reopen; accepted, uncertain and resent operations fire nothing; an agent that has left the team is not fired for that team's goal; a feed answer naming an unknown session or another machine is refused before any event; and the walk is bounded: with 1,000 unrelated goals and teams that hold no compaction reminder, none is visited, counted by an observable probe. The handback states the cost per confirmed compaction, and names what happens if a holder loses team membership between the authority recheck and the append, and why that is harmless; if it is not, the window is closed (Brisket 59c87b10; Waffles ad4d79dc).

amendments.subject: Amendment 33 made precise: the compaction holder walk may run the existing borrowed membership predicates on each holder team; it copies no list and scans no other team
amendments.ruling: Amendment 33 said no member list is read in the compaction holder walk. TeamStore::team is an indexed, borrowed point read, but a team's members and held entries are vectors (teams_state.rs), and the existing current-recipient check judges membership with members.iter().any and held.iter().any on that borrowed team, so each holder team's current entries are visited (Brisket dc521908). The sentence means: no member list or team catalogue is copied, no team other than a current compaction holder is visited, and no change log or history is read. The existing borrowed membership predicates stay, and TeamStore is not written or widened. The handback states the cost per confirmed compaction as the number of compaction team holders visited and, for each, the current member and held entries examined, measured at 10 and 1,000 holders. That membership is a linear check over a vector joins amendment 33's FOUND on TeamStore's missing reverse member index. The recheck-to-append window is answered: an Evented records a confirmed observation and makes a reminder due, but grants no delivery; the dispatcher selects current team members and rechecks recipient authority before any pipe write, so a member removed after the recheck receives nothing, and the revoked-member test proves it (Brisket dc521908).

amendments.subject: R4: a confirmed compaction's events are written as one batch, one Evented per eligible holder plus a completion marker, with one durable flush
amendments.ruling: A confirmed compaction keeps one Evented for each eligible holder and then one final Evented naming no holder, whose stable id is derived from the confirmed operation. The marker records that the confirmation has been applied, so the same confirmation answered again fires nothing, including for a holder added after it (Brisket 9ce3f8d8). Writing those H+1 leaves one at a time would cost H+1 syncs, about 1,001 at 1,000 holders. Under Tom's storage rule (a batch is one durable operation with one flush, never leaf by leaf), goals_store/control.rs writes them as one FrontierLog::append_batch: one ordinary sync, or three at the existing snapshot boundary, folded only after the append succeeds. The leaves keep the existing Evented format; the existing reader must accept an Evented naming no holder, and the fold treats it only as the completion marker. An uncertain append is settled by the existing owner: after a reopen the store holds all H+1 leaves or none of them, never some, verified before the confirmation is acknowledged, and an unapplied confirmation can be applied again under the same stable ids without a duplicate. Tests: a confirmation with 1,000 holders costs exactly one sync outside a snapshot boundary; the same confirmation answered again, live and after a reopen, fires nothing, including for a holder added after the first answer; a batch interrupted before its sync leaves all of its leaves or none after a reopen, and re-applying it fires each holder exactly once in total; a batch that crosses SNAPSHOT_EVERY costs three syncs and holds every leaf; a goals log written before this box opens unchanged. The handback states the sync count at H = 10 and H = 1,000, measured with lys-log-store's flush-counts feature as for the audit store (Brisket 9ce3f8d8; Waffles adaf4966).

amendments.subject: PROPOSAL, not yet ruled: a harness version is qualified by a recorded, person-made qualification act in the installed product, never by a compiled list or a bypass
amendments.ruling: THE CIRCLE. Amendment 8 makes qualification R6's proof, pinning the adapter and the version the harness reports of itself. But lys-runner harness_control/process.rs:26 holds QUALIFIED = &[], and spawn (lines 235 to 246) refuses every version control_adapter_unqualified before the child exists. The installed product can therefore never produce the proof that would let it launch, and Tom's rule that everything is written before the one install rules out adding pins after the window (Brisket ad32b651; Waffles 4a9e335d). Read on Tom's Mac at 02:35: claude reports 2.1.291 (Claude Code) and codex reports codex-cli 0.159.2. 1. WHERE THE EVIDENCE COMES FROM. Only from the installed candidate on Tom's Mac, in Waffles' window, using the machine's own signed-in claude and codex (Tom, 3 October: no CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR unless a person chose it; no copied credentials). No machine qualifies earlier: a turn, a compaction and a stop need a signed-in harness, and Dean's harnesses are not signed in, and must not be by copying credentials. No test runs on the Mac outside the window. 2. RECORDED, NOT COMPILED. QUALIFIED stops being a compiled list. The runner keeps a qualification record in its own durable store, one entry per (adapter, self-reported version), each holding the evidence digest, the person who made the act and the instant. An entry is written only by a qualification act: an administrator, signed in as a person, asks for it by name for one adapter on one machine. The act runs exactly one launch through the real adapter and the runner-owned pipes. It is the same spawn path, marked as a qualification and refused for any other use. The act proves, in order: the init frame's self-reported version (Claude system/init, Codex initialize answer); one reminder admitted under its correlation; one real compaction with its evidence and matching turn completion; one stop with the process exit observed. Only when all four are observed is the entry written, in one durable operation. Any missing step writes nothing and names the step. Every other managed launch reads the record and refuses an unrecorded (adapter, version) control_adapter_unqualified by name. A version change, such as a harness update, is unrecorded until it is qualified again. Nothing is inferred from a fixture, a sha256 or a version list. 3. WHAT THE WINDOW PROVES. The installed candidate refuses a managed start of qual-box20 before qualification, control_adapter_unqualified. The administrator's two qualification acts record claude 2.1.291 and codex-cli 0.159.2, each with its four observed steps. The same managed start then succeeds, and Stage B (Archie's script) runs: the browser-set threshold and reminder persist after reload, the turn-boundary delivery, the context crossing, the real compaction and the stop, for both harnesses. The refusal of an unrecorded version is proved on Dean with a fixture executable reporting another version, never live. amendments.subject: R6: QUALIFIED stays a compiled list, filled before the one battery and install by a pin commit citing Stage A's evidence; the init frame is the qualification proof and the pre-spawn --version only a first refusal; amendment 36's proposal is withdrawn

amendments.subject: R5: a boundary decision's journal records are one explicit writer batch with one sync, unconditionally; replaces amendment 39's measured condition; R5 gains lys-runner durable.rs
amendments.ruling: operations.jsonl appends sync through lys-runner durable.rs (std::fs::File::sync_data at line 175, inside the per-path write loop), not lys-log-store, so lys-log-store's flush-counts cannot count them. The writer coalesces up to 32 queued commands opportunistically, with no transaction boundary, so scheduler timing can split one decision across syncs (Brisket 5bb22571). A measurement of one sync could therefore pass by luck, and a crash between the two halves of one decision would leave part of it on disk. Amendment 39's "if either takes more than one" is replaced: the explicit single-command batch is built now, whatever R = 0 and R = 5 measure, and the measurement is the proof of the batch (Waffles bfcbb001). R5 gains durable.rs, read on main at 181 lines (Waffles bfcbb001). It also gains lys-runner's Cargo.toml, only if the counter uses a feature. THE BATCH, as Brisket directed: one bounded writer batch slot is reserved on the first successfully validated journal record, before any metadata or controller mutation; that decision's journal bytes accumulate in operations/store.rs and are submitted once, as one durable operation with one sync. A failed or dropped non-empty batch names a writer failure and blocks pipe writes. A pre-enqueue offset or queue refusal keeps the existing red's unchanged authority and retry. There is no sync and no whole Table clone under the Table lock, and the feed stays with its existing owner. The touched files are durable.rs plus the already-owned operations/store.rs, operations.rs, harness_control/context.rs and the events.rs fixture. THE COUNTER: a per-writer, per-path sync count compiled only under cfg(test) or under a lys-runner feature named flush-counts, as lys-log-store names its own. No production code path changes for it. TESTS: one boundary decision with R = 0 and D = 1, and one with R = 5 and D = 1, each measures exactly one operations.jsonl sync; a decision interrupted inside its batch reopens with all of its records or none; two decisions queued together still produce two whole decisions, never a mixed record. The handback states both measured counts.

amendments.subject: R5: a same-ID retry is compared with a private digest of the original complete typed request, kept in the v2 journal with its held outcome
amendments.ruling: operations/delivery.rs accept compares a same-ID retry's session, request name and original text digest, but omits GoalReminder.reference and ContextCompact.crossing. The currently prepared reference can change under boundary authority, so the current preparation cannot establish what the original request was (Brisket 91ea995e). Accepted as proposed. First acceptance keeps a private SHA-256 of the original complete typed request in the v2 journal record and in the borrowed checkpoint, indexed only while that outcome is retained. The digest is taken over one canonical encoding of the typed request: fixed field order, no map iteration order, the same bytes on every platform and after a reopen. A unit test pins one known request to its known digest. Later records of the operation carry the digest unchanged. A same-ID retry is compared with it before the held outcome is returned. A retry whose request differs in any field, reference and crossing included, is refused as a reused operation by name, and nothing about the original is revealed. The public text digest and receipts are unchanged. Pruning removes the private digest with its held outcome, and the spent-ID refusal stays permanent. The installed v1 migration sets the digest absent and keeps the existing text, name and session checks. v1's formats cannot contain these managed request variants, and a test proves that a migrated v1 operation retried with the same text is still answered as before. The v2 shape is still draft-only (amendment 41) and changes in place, with no v2 migration. Red: a changed goal reference and a changed crossing are each refused, live and after a reopen, while an unchanged retry returns the same held outcome despite a changed current preparation. Cost: one SHA-256 over one small request at first acceptance, and one 32-byte comparison per retry. No sync, scan or history read is added. Files: operations.rs, operations/control.rs, operations/store.rs, operations/delivery.rs, tests/operations_index/cases.rs and tests/control_recovery.rs, all already R5's.

amendments.subject: R5: amendment 44 completed; the request digest's canonical encoding is named in the code, and a v1 record of each managed kind is proved impossible or refused

The digest is taken over one canonical encoding of the typed request: field order and integer forms fixed, no display text. That encoding is named in the code as one function the digest alone uses. 2. A test shows that the same request yields the same digest after a reopen, beside amendment 44's known-digest test. 3. The v1 migration's absent identity is correct only because v1 cannot hold these managed variants. So a test proves, for each managed request kind (GoalReminder, ContextCompact and every other variant this box adds to the operation request), that a v1 record of that kind cannot be constructed or is refused by name at migration. amendments.subject: FOUND, not in this box: the runner's used-ID set only ever grows; its measured cost is recorded and its fix is briefed on its own as DIRECTORY-084
amendments.ruling: crates/lys-runner/src/operations.rs keeps every operation ID it has ever seen in `seen` (main 3d72f2e9 line 174, inserted at 310, checked at 355; the same roles at 212, 245 and 324 in the draft). prune (343 to 352) drops an expired outcome but never its ID, and repeated (354 to 362) refuses operation_repeated only by finding the ID in `seen`. No operation ID carries a time, so an expired ID can be told from a new one only by keeping it, and dropping it would let a stale replay run a second time (Archie 20b1c786, confirmed by Brisket cbbbc991: an_expired_operation_id_is_refused_after_a_restart, tests/operations_index/cases.rs 94 to 109, passes only through seen.contains). The set is older than this box, and this box does not make it grow faster, so this box does not change it (Waffles d84942a7). It is Tom's no-pruning failure all the same and is recorded here as FOUND, not deferred. Measured on the draft's typed checkpoint, one release fixture per population with 1000 retained operations and an empty tail (Brisket e8d905bf, run b113ff3a; observations, not bounds): at 1k used IDs the checkpoint is 1.6 MB, the Table is held 3.5 ms and startup takes 5.1 ms; at 10k, 2.0 MB, 2.5 ms and 5.7 ms; at 100k, 6.1 MB, 11.5 ms and 13.0 ms; at 1m, 46.6 MB, 146.6 ms and 208.5 ms. Every checkpoint serializes the whole set under the Table, so the hold grows with every ID ever used, for good. The fix is its own brief, written by hand on main as DIRECTORY-084: each operation ID carries its issue time, an ID older than the retention window or dated too far ahead is refused by its age, `seen` is pruned in the existing expiry pass, and the old random-only IDs are retired once by a named migration. It goes to Tom in the morning note as found, with that fix written. Nothing in this box claims the guard harmless or bounded.

amendments.subject: R2, R6: Claude binds by the documented initialize handshake with no turn; init stays the version proof at the first turn; no clock wait; the protocol failure is reported whole and apart from cleanup
amendments.ruling: Stage A at e8d905bf proved 0 of 2 (Waffles 6608ca3c). Claude Code 2.1.292 deadlocked: Controller::bootstrap sends nothing for Claude (harness_control.rs 191 to 194), so the example waits for control_bound from system/init, and Claude in --print stream-json mode sends init only after input. Waffles measured this with stdin held open and no input: hook frames only, never init (c4d1b06e). The harness documents it. @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.292, whose claudeCodeVersion is 2.1.292 (sdk.d.ts as published on unpkg, read 7 October), says SDKSystemMessage subtype init is "Session metadata the CLI emits at the start of each turn" and carries claude_code_version (lines 5944 to 5950). It documents the control handshake that needs no turn as SDKControlInitializeRequest {subtype: 'initialize'} (line 4477), answered by SDKControlInitializeResponse (line 4564), which carries no version. Ruled: 1. Binding. For Claude, Controller::bootstrap's Update writes one control_request with subtype initialize and a fresh request_id, carrying no hooks, servers, prompt or agents. claude.rs binds the transport when the control_response with that request_id answers success. An error answer, or a control_response with any other request_id, is refused by name. Nothing from the response body (account, models, commands, agents, output styles) is kept, logged or written. Only its arrival and its request_id are recorded. The product and the example take the same path, because the deadlock is the product's as well. 2. Version proof. Init stays the proof (amendment 37), observed at the first admitted turn, which in the qualifier is the reminder. Its claude_code_version must equal version_report, or the harness is refused by name and that turn is recorded refused. For Codex the proof stays the initialize result (codex.rs 256). For both harnesses the pinned version is the version the serving process reports in that frame, never the CLI's --version alone. If a different process serves (Waffles' lead c5c4aaa6: a 0.160.1 app-server daemon beside codex-cli 0.159.2), the two differ and the harness is refused by name. 3. Evidence order becomes launcher, version_report, bound {correlation}, reminder_admitted, init {version}, compaction, stop, terminal_writes. The writer emits the steps in this order whenever each was observed. Both fixtures are rewritten to it, and the battery's fixture check and Archie's judge follow. 4. No clock. The brief forbids request timeouts and watchdogs (boundaries), and that holds in the example too. A named failure replaces the hang: every wait in the example ends on the frame it awaits, on the child's exit, or on EOF of its output, each written as observed:false with its reason. The example never waits for a frame the harness documents as answering input it has not sent. The red is a fake Claude that, as 2.1.292 does, sends init only after input: at e8d905bf it never binds, and after the change it binds on the initialize answer with no turn sent. The red asserts on the frames written, never on elapsed time. A person's stop stays qualification_cancelled. 5. Failure reporting. qualify_adapter.rs 310 to 313 folds the protocol error into the cleanup error, and Codex's reason was lost (Stage A printed qualification_cleanup_failed with an empty reason). The protocol error is written first, in full, as the failed step's reason: its name and its words. Cleanup's result follows in its own member, cleanup: ok, or its own name and words. An empty reason or empty cleanup is a writer defect and refused by name. fail-stop-red gains a line showing both. 6. Codex reproduction. Brisket reproduces the Codex failure with codex-cli 0.159.2 on the Dean seat, or names where it can be reproduced, after item 5 and before changing any Codex path. No seat's app-server daemon, ~/.codex or any credential is touched or read. A Codex defect found there is a scope request, not a change under this amendment. Paths: harness_control.rs, harness_control/claude.rs, tests/harness_claude.rs, examples/qualify_adapter.rs, examples/qualify_adapter/owned.rs and the two qualifier fixtures, all already this box's. Checks on the own Dean seat before the new candidate is handed to Waffles, judged by parsed output with 0 failed: the red at e8d905bf quoted, then lys-runner whole nextest, cargo test --doc -p lys-runner, fmt, clippy in both configurations, ast-grep, the length scan, and the qualify_adapter example built. Stop and post, changing nothing further, if 2.1.292 answers initialize with an error or not at all, or if the reproduction points outside these paths. The new candidate is a new commit on box20-wip whose parent is e8d905bf. Stage A runs again from the start against it, and nothing is pinned from the failed run.

amendments.subject: the issuer challenge solver allocates nothing per counter, and the sign-in names its refusals by cause
amendments.ruling: The battery at 43ac58a9 went red on the identity leg (Waffles 67ac1803): the product sign-in after the install answered 401 SignInRefused where 200 was expected (lys tests product.rs 81). Read from the leg log and the pinned Rauthy (Brisket 0f875493, Archie): that attempt's POST /auth/v1/pow came at 03:31:31.452 and its POST /auth/v1/oidc/authorize at 03:32:05.664, 34.2 s later. The challenge expires 30 s after issue (vendor/rauthy config.toml [pow] exp, rauthy_config.rs 590-593; Lys sets no override). Rauthy validates the challenge before the password (api/src/oidc.rs 343-344) and answers a challenge error 403 Forbidden (error_impls.rs 444-448), logged at debug only. That authorize was answered in 874 us and no "Invalid user credentials" line was logged for it. The failed-login delay (service/src/login_delay.rs 74-96) sleeps from the third failure and blacklists from the fifth; this run had one failure, the test's deliberate wrong password at 03:31:31.159. So the delay did not refuse it. An expired challenge is supported, not proven, because Lys kept neither the status nor the body of the answer. sign_in.rs 294 maps every 4xx but 429 to SignInRefused, so whatever the cause, the person was told their password was wrong. Ruling (Waffles 6638f87b), in three parts, all in R6. 1. The solver. solve (sign_in.rs 191) formats a new String and hashes the whole challenge on every counter. It hashes the challenge prefix once and, for each counter, clones that hasher state, writes the counter's decimal digits into a fixed stack buffer and finishes the clone. There is no allocation and no formatting inside the search. The one answer String is built after the counter is found. The answer is unchanged: the challenge followed by the decimal counter, and the existing solve tests pass unchanged. Red: a unit test in src/sign_in_tests.rs solves a difficulty-19 challenge through a crate-private counter search and counts the allocations made inside it, which must be 0. At main the same count is above 0. There is no wall-clock assertion. Counting needs a global allocator, which needs unsafe code, and the workspace denies unsafe_code (Cargo.toml 98). An integration test cannot reach a crate-private routine, so the red is a unit test, and the routine is not made public for it. The counter is a maintained allocation-counting crate taken as a dev-dependency of lys-identity-server only, with its unsafe inside the dependency, as Cargo.toml 52 does for the terminal. It is pinned exactly in Cargo.lock, which changes for it alone, and its name, version and licence are named in the commit and the handback (Waffles 9575481a). The pin is allocation-counter =0.8.1, MIT or Apache-2.0, with no dependencies of its own, read from Dean's registry cache (Brisket 901ce1d2). It must not appear in the non-dev dependency graph of any released binary, and cargo tree -e normal shows that in the handback. No lint is weakened and no allow is added. If no such crate offers a safe measuring call, the builder stops and names it, and does not write unsafe code. 2. Refusals by cause. accepted (sign_in.rs 275), which the password and provider sign-ins share (sign_in_upstream.rs 213), maps by what the issuer said. 401 whose JSON error word is Unauthorized, Rauthy's answer for a wrong email or password (data/src/entity/users.rs 2019-2033, api/src/oidc.rs 385-388), and only that answer, is SignInRefused. 429 stays SignInThrottled and 200 stays SecondFactorUnsupported. A new refusal, IssuerChallengeExpired, answers 503 with the reason that the sign-in service's challenge expired before it was answered and that pressing sign in again starts a new one. It is refused in two places. First, after solving and before the credentials are posted, when Lys's clock is at or past the challenge's own expires field (unix seconds, the third field), so no password is sent with a dead challenge. Second, when the authorize answer is 403 and Lys's clock is then at or past that expires field. A second new refusal, IssuerRefused {status, error}, covers any other 4xx. It answers 502 with the issuer's status and the issuer's JSON error word, or "unreadable" when the body is not Rauthy's error JSON. Nothing else is kept from the answer: never its message, the email, the password, the challenge or a token. Both new refusals are logged at warn with the same fields, so the next such failure can be diagnosed from the log. Red, in tests/sign_in_page.rs against its fixture issuer, failing at main and passing at the head. amendments.subject: the runner fixture's boundary service sets its end flag under the table lock, so its waiter cannot miss the wake
amendments.ruling: In the full workspace nextest at 98f0e035 on Annabel, harness_control::events::tests::channel_loss_releases_human_waiters_refuses_more_input_and_ends_its_child ran for 15 min 23 s without ending. It was ended by SIGTERM, which is not a verdict. The same test passed in the 3603/3603 run at c02034a6 on Tom's Mac. Brisket's bounded stack sample (checks/workspace-runner-wait.sample.txt, SHA256 60ed6b68...b1959) shows the test body had returned. The test thread is in the fixture's Service::drop (events.rs 569-580), joining the worker. The worker, fixture-boundary-service, is in Sessions::until_any (session/control.rs 20-35) blocked in Condvar::wait (session.rs 390). until_any checks its flag while holding the table lock, then waits, and the wait releases the lock atomically. Service::drop stores ended and calls notify_all without taking that lock. When the store and the notify fall between the worker's check and its wait, the wake is lost and the worker sleeps for ever. In R6: Service::drop stores ended while holding the table lock (taken through Sessions::lock), releases it, then wakes, and then joins. That is the pattern the production sites already use: change under the lock, then wake (session.rs 245-249, collector/stop.rs 34-35). The production Runtime::drop (events.rs 52-58) has the same flag-then-wake shape. A waiter can hold a Runtime's left flag only through the one clone at harness_control/approval.rs 48, and that clone is taken from a Runtime looked up in the table. So the drop is safe if every Runtime that has been installed in the table is dropped while the table lock is held. The builder confirms that with file:line for each place an installed Runtime leaves the table. If one is dropped outside the lock, the builder stops and names it rather than changing it. One ordinary case is permitted and named here. A start that is cancelled after run(plan) prepared it, because the runner is stopping or the generation moved on, drops a Runtime that was never installed (session/lifecycle.rs 500-505, Prepared::drop at 137-145, Spawned.control at 124-130, built by session/lifecycle/managed.rs 49-75). Nothing can hold its flag, so no wake can be lost; Brisket found it while auditing. The hand-back names it as that permitted case. A second permitted case is the final destruction of Sessions and its Mutex<Table> (session.rs 232-234, 339-343), which drops every Runtime still in the table with exclusive ownership instead of a guard. The one clone of left (approval.rs 48) is paired with an Arc<Sessions> clone (49) moved into the same worker (55-57), so no waiter can exist while the last owner is destroyed. Brisket found it in the source audit (SOURCE-AUDIT.md at c02034a6). Amendment 70's TLS read is answered by the same audit: the server's own provider probe client (sign_in_providers.rs 212) makes https requests to provider authorization endpoints (353-360). So lys-identity-server declares features = ["json", "rustls-tls"], the feature name lys-secrets already uses. The red is the sampled hang at 98f0e035; a lost wake cannot be forced without a hook in production code, and none is added. The green is that test under nextest in the full workspace nextest at the new head. This part goes on the same branch as amendment 70 (from c02034a6) and is proven by the same exact-head run. No other change.
